hook_text: 1 kg 50 g is 150 g. True or false? Think of a bag of sugar.
clip_script: Kroonstad, baking for the school bake sale. 1 kilogram is 1 000 grams. 3 kg of potatoes? 3 000 g. 1 kg 50 g? 1 000 plus 50: 1 050 g, not 150. A quarter of a kilogram: 250 g, one block of butter. The flour bag says 2 and 1/2 kg: that is 2 500 g. Scones need 500 g a batch: 5 batches. 1 kg of sugar, use 350 g: 650 g left. Change to grams, then bake the numbers.
visual_style: Flour pouring from a big bag into bowls of 500 g each, counting five batches.
mood: Warm and homely, like a kitchen full of baking smells.
pacing: The 150 g trap, the quarter kilogram, then the batches.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the mass in grams on three packets at home.
